name: CloudBrowser AI

modes.label: Browser-hour overage unpublished
modes.note: Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Basic
plans.note: 30,000 units/month; one unit is 30 seconds per open tab (nominally 250 single-tab hours), so two tabs for one minute consume four units; 10 instances and 3 tabs per instance.

plans.name: Premium
plans.note: 120,000 units/month; one unit is 30 seconds per open tab (nominally 1,000 single-tab hours), so concurrent tabs consume units separately; 25 instances and 3 tabs per instance.

plans.name: Basic annual
plans.note: $250/year billed yearly; no free trial; 30,000 per-tab usage units monthly.

plans.name: Premium annual
plans.note: $900/year billed yearly; no free trial; 120,000 per-tab usage units monthly.

free.conditions: Seven-day free trial applies to monthly Basic; annual plans are billed yearly and do not include a free trial. All paid plans advertise a 14-day money-back guarantee.

features.ip_note: 'Premium proxies' included on every plan (type not stated); bring your own proxy supported; no per-GB price.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Premium proxies included in plan feature list, but no published bandwidth allowance/overage found. Do not translate to unlimitedGB or $0/GB.
Saved cookies/local Storage supported; live remote desktop is browser viewing, not proof of full general-purpose Linux desktop. Docs/pricing paths resolved to same homepage.

fleet.tiers: Entry Basic 10; Premium 25; custom concurrent instances by contact.
fleet.notes: A seven-day trial is offered, but its specific concurrent-browser allocation is not explicit; default remains null. Basic supports 10, while 50/300/1,000 need custom terms.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.note: Complete HTTP API is Open / Close / Start+Stop Remote Desktop / Get Browsers / Session List / Session Remove; no endpoint to take a snapshot or checkpoint, and saved sessions cannot be forked into new machines beyond cookie/localStorage restore.

harness_api.note: Nothing runs an agent inside the browser container. The MCP server (18 browser tools) lets EXTERNAL agents (ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor) drive the browser; 'AI Functions' are stateless LLM calls on HTML (query/summarize/to-JSON), not a harness.

guest_firewall.note: Managed Chrome in a per-browser container; users get only CDP / remote desktop, no shell or root, so nothing like nftables can be configured.

volume_attach.note: Browser-as-a-service with no storage/volume API; only saved sessions (cookies/localStorage) persist.

volume_shared.note: No volumes. A saved session (label) can be recovered by later browsers, but that is cookie/localStorage restore, not a shared mounted filesystem.

isolation.quote: The service is designed to operate in a containerized environment, ensuring scalability and reliability. Each browser runs in its own container, isolated from others.

image_oci.quote: This endpoint allows you to open a browser with advanced configurations, including custom browser arguments, custom proxy settings, and more.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Open Browser only exposes Chrome/Chromium args, headless, stealth, proxy and session flags — no custom Docker/OCI image parameter.

docker_inside.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud so ChatGPT, Claude and your own agents can browse, click, type and pull data from any website
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Users get a managed Chrome/CDP endpoint or remote desktop, never a shell inside the container.

nested_virt.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No shell/root or hypervisor access is exposed inside the browser container.

desktop.quote: start_remote_desktop - Starts VNC access to a browser
desktop.note: Live remote desktop (VNC-based) streaming of the browser session is included on every plan.

ssh.quote: Give your AI agents a real browser.
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Access is via CDP WebSocket endpoint or live remote desktop only; no SSH to the underlying machine.

snapshot.quote: saveSession: If true, the browser session is saved periodically and at the end, cookies and local storage, but not the open tabs.
snapshot.note: Only cookies/localStorage are saved and restored (saveSession/recoverSession); there is no disk or memory snapshot of the machine itself.

snapshot_auto.quote: saveSession: If true, the browser session is saved periodically and at the end, cookies and local storage, but not the open tabs.
snapshot_auto.note: There is no automatic full machine/VM state snapshot on stop; periodic saveSession only persists cookies/localStorage, and only when the flag is explicitly enabled.

fork.quote: Open Browser, Close Browser, Get Browsers, Get Saved Sessions, Remove Saved Session
fork.note: No clone/fork endpoint exists; only opening new independent browsers or restoring a saved cookie/localStorage session.

fork_running.quote: Open Browser, Close Browser, Get Browsers, Get Saved Sessions, Remove Saved Session
fork_running.note: No API to clone a running browser without stopping it.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Open Browser, Close Browser, Get Browsers, Get Saved Sessions, Remove Saved Session
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork capability at all, so cloning with live memory/processes is not possible.

pause_resume.quote: keepOpen: Seconds of inactivity before the browser automatically closes.
pause_resume.note: There is only close (destroy) after an idle timeout, no pause/resume of a running browser instance.

wake_on_request.quote: Users send an HTTP request to our service's API to create a browser. ... the service configures and launches a new instance of a web browser.
wake_on_request.note: Browsers are freshly created synchronously per Open request; there is no sleeping/stopped instance that wakes on an inbound request.

persistent_disk.quote: saveSession: ... cookies and local storage, but not the open tabs.
persistent_disk.note: Only cookies/localStorage persist via saveSession/recoverSession; there is no general persistent filesystem/disk that survives stop/start.

auto_stop_idle.quote: keepOpen: Seconds of inactivity before the browser automatically closes. The value 0 is never, default is 300 seconds.

live_resize.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CPU/RAM sizing parameter exists at all for the abstracted browser container.

agent_harnesses.quote: Add CloudBrowser once and your assistant gets 18 browser tools — in chat, in your editor or inside your own agents.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. CloudBrowser exposes browser-automation tools for EXTERNAL agents/harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) to call; it does not preinstall or template a coding agent harness inside its own machines.

own_agent_api.quote: Currently, only OpenAI is supported as the AI provider. ... Every request must include an openAIConfiguration object ... apiKey: Your OpenAI API key.
own_agent_api.note: AI Functions is a pass-through wrapper that calls OpenAI with the caller's own API key to summarize/extract page content; it is not a first-party autonomous browser/computer-use agent driven by a CloudBrowser API.

lang_node.note: First-party Node.js client library, plus Node.js quickstart examples.

public_ipv4.quote: We provide a list of IP addresses from our shared fleet for whitelisting purposes.
public_ipv4.note: Browsers are reached through a shared load-balanced fleet endpoint, not a dedicated public IPv4 per machine.

inbound_https.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The service exposes a CDP WebSocket endpoint to control the browser, not a general HTTPS ingress to arbitrary ports on the machine.

ingress_rules.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. There is no exposed port surface to apply ingress/allowlist rules to.

egress_allowlist.quote: proxy: Custom proxy configuration. If not specified, the service will use an automatically assigned proxy.
egress_allowlist.note: Only outbound proxy selection (bring-your-own or provider-assigned) exists; no allow/deny list or no-internet mode for outbound traffic.

egress_http_rules.quote: proxy: Custom proxy configuration. If not specified, the service will use an automatically assigned proxy.
egress_http_rules.note: No method/path-level outbound HTTP rules are offered, only whole-session proxy routing.

secret_proxy.note: API keys (e.g. OpenAI) are passed directly in the request body; no first-party credential-injection proxy for arbitrary HTTP APIs was found.

static_egress_ip.quote: Custom: Custom browser hours, Custom concurrent instances, Dedicated proxies, Live remote desktop, Dedicated support manager
static_egress_ip.note: Only the Custom/enterprise plan advertises 'dedicated proxies', implying a fixed outbound IP; Basic and Premium share 'premium proxies' with no dedicated-IP guarantee.

gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No GPU machine option exists; the product only sizes by browser-hours/concurrency.

windows.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only a managed Chrome/Chromium browser is offered, never a full Windows desktop machine.

macos.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only a managed Chrome/Chromium browser is offered, never a macOS machine.

self_host.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Only a hosted SaaS API/dashboard is offered; no self-hosted package.

byoc.quote: We use load balancing to distribute traffic to all our workers located in Amsterdam.
byoc.note: Workers run only on CloudBrowser's own fleet (Amsterdam, with US/Asia planned); no bring-your-own-cloud deployment option is offered.

open_source.quote: The open-source MCP connector is free, and it adds no AI inference charge. Browser usage requires a CloudBrowser account and a paid plan after the 7-day Basic trial.
open_source.note: Only the thin MCP connector is open source; the core browser-hosting platform/backend is closed-source and metered.

sso.quote: Sign in with your CloudBrowser account (OAuth) or send your API token as a Bearer header.
sso.note: Sign-in is via the provider's own OAuth for the MCP connector or an API token; no SAML/OIDC enterprise SSO for the account/dashboard is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: We use load balancing to distribute traffic to all our workers located in Amsterdam.
eu_data_residency.note: All current workers/browsers run in Amsterdam (EU); there is no region selector, so EU residency is the default and only option today (US/Asia expansion is only planned).

max_session_h.quote: keepOpen: Seconds of inactivity before the browser automatically closes. The value 0 is never, default is 300 seconds.
max_session_h.note: keepOpen governs an idle timeout (default 300s, settable to 0 for never); no separate absolute maximum session duration is documented, so a session can in principle run indefinitely if kept active.

arm64.quote: CloudBrowser runs real Chrome in the cloud so ChatGPT, Claude and your own agents can browse, click, type and pull data from any website
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — CloudBrowser is a managed-Chrome browser-automation service with no machine/instance architecture selection (no CPU/arch option is exposed anywhere in the docs, pricing, or API), so an ARM64 choice does not apply.
